<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above -->

#### Description
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->
- Move Auxiliary data filtering to the top of the enumeration stack to allow aux data to flow through all subscriptions so they can to be notified of delistings/splits/dividends/etc.

#### Related Issue
<!--- This project only accepts pull requests related to open issues -->
<!--- If suggesting a new feature or change, please discuss it in an issue first -->
<!--- If fixing a bug, there should be an issue describing it with steps to reproduce -->
<!--- Please link to the issue here: -->
Closes #5422
Closes #5447 

#### Motivation and Context
<!--- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? -->
The issues above highlighted an issue where delisted contracts were still emitting past expiration, upon inspection it became clear that the enumerators they used (FF) relied on the flow of Aux data through the enumerator to end the subscription after delisting. This flow was cut off in #4828 to stop multiple aux points for the same security & time entering the timeslice factory.

Now we refactored this solution to allow the data to flow all the way to the top of the enumeration stack where we will filter it using a similar strategy before emitting.

#### Requires Documentation Change
<!--- Please indicate if these changes will require updates to documentation, and if so, specify what changes are required -->
N/A

#### How Has This Been Tested?
<!--- Please describe in detail how you tested your changes. -->
<!--- Include details of your testing environment, and the tests you ran to -->
<!--- see how your change affects other areas of the code, etc. -->
- Added regressions for Options & Futures showing we no longer receive expired contracts the day after expiration
- Added unit tests asserting filtering behavior on `SubscriptionDataEnumerator` and `SubscriptionUtils.CreateAndScheduleWorker` (where I implemented the filters)

review_comments:
hm sure about moving next here? We are not using `_enumerator.Current` 🤔 
Why is `ShouldEmitAuxiliaryData` public?

Yeah I used `MoveNext()` there because we are explicitly skipping `_enumerator.Current` because it is Aux data that shouldn't be emitted. That way we just move right past it without the caller knowing any better. 

Its like in `SubscriptionUtils.CreateAndScheduleWorker` where I continue if the data is aux and we shouldn't emit, it just repeats the loop and MovesNext() again effectively skipping the aux data.

1 -> 4
there are internal subscriptions to aux data (splits/dividend/delisting)

Cool! We should have a secondary assert to make sure OnData was actually called with data, we usually do this opening a position in the related security but it could also be through some assert in OnAlgorithmEnded I think, the same comment about the option regression algorithm
